extracted.intended_audience: Governor and Council at Fort St. George (British East India Company officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for deciding outstanding territorial, revenue, and infrastructure disputes between the Nabob of Arcot and the Rajah of Tanjore, with reference to the treaty of 1762 and the 38th section of the act of Parliament. Directs local officials how to investigate, adjudicate, apply remedies, and when to suspend action and report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on Rajah's contribution for war expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not insist upon any demands upon the Rajah for the expenses of the late war beyond the sum of four lacs of pagodas annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: insisting on larger demands might interrupt harmony between the Company and the Rajah and impede the general system in place. The instruction is explicit: restrict claims to avoid political friction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and preserve Nabob's just claim to arrears (peshcush)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nabob's just claim on the Rajah for arrears of peshcush is not to be affected; the Company should not neglect that just claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance: encourage the Nabob to allow those arrears (and future payments) to be received by the Company and carried in discharge of his debt to the Company; convince him that, once discharged, Company will exert itself to ensure regular payment into his hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate means to collect arrears consistent with Rajah's resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use all proper means to bring arrears to account as soon as possible, but do so consistently with due attention to the present state of the Rajah's resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the three-year proposal for receipt of arrears is inconsistent with the Rajah's resources, local officials must temper enforcement and adopt measures that do not exceed capacity; discretion and prudence are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation under the 38th section (treaty-centered adjudication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 38th section of the act, only indeterminate rights and pretensions that are properly connected with the treaty of 1762 should be taken into immediate consideration and settled under its terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical test: identify whether a disputed point is 'immediately connected' with the treaty of 1762. If it falls outside the treaty's purposes (e.g., not contemplated by contracting parties), it should not be treated as part of the strict duties imposed by that section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated points to investigate and decide
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and decide the following points: (1) whether the jaghire of Arnee belongs to the Nabob, the Rajah, or the descendants of Tremaul Row; (2) whether the fort/district of Hanamantagoody (in the Marawar) ought to be possessed by the Nabob or delivered to the Rajah; (3) to whom the government share of the Tanjore 1775–6 crop properly belongs; (4) whether the Rajah has a right or ought to be permitted to repair parts of the Anicut / Cavery banks lying within Trichinopoly and to take earth/sand therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain a 'complete knowledge of the facts and circumstances' relative to each point and determine their connection (if any) with the treaty of 1762 before settling them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arnee — requirement of satisfactory title/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not comply with the Rajah's request for Arnee unless records furnish satisfactory information of the Rajah's title or the degree of relationship/connection with the Killadar of Arnee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the research offers no evidence in support of the Rajah's claim, compliance is inappropriate. However, the Commissioners also recognize the hereditary right of Tremaul Row's descendants under the 1762 stipulations — so balance lack of proof against treaty stipulations (see restoration to heir below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arnee — restoration of heir of Tremaul Row unless forfeited
rubrics_metrics.description: If the heir of Tremaul Row is not in possession and has not forfeited the jaghire by violation of treaty or disobedience, he is to be forthwith restored to possession according to the treaty of 1762.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the Governor judges that strong reasons of peace and tranquillity require suspension of restoration, he may suspend execution but must transmit full proceedings, facts, and reasons to higher authority with all convenient speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hanamantagoody — deference to Nabob's possession absent proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Nabob is in actual possession and the records do not satisfactorily demonstrate the Rajah's 1762 possession, do not dispossess the Nabob of Hanamantagoody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Nabob's long-continued claim and current possession are weighty; absent documentary proof to the contrary, local officials are not warranted in granting the Rajah's request to dispossess the Nabob.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government share of the 1775–6 crop — de facto sovereign's right and limits on demands
rubrics_metrics.description: The government share of the 1776 crop belonged to the de facto sovereign (the Nabob) because he was then in full and absolute possession; assignments made by him of that share are valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the same time, do not make further demands upon the Rajah regarding parts of the government share collected by his people or long-ago balances — after such a length of time it would be highly unjust to compel accounting or payment beyond what the Rajah admits. The Rajah should not be held accountable for more than what he acknowledges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling the Rajah's one lac deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The one lac of pagodas deposited by the Rajah on account of the Nabob's claims should not be applied until it can be properly disposed of consistent with principles of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local officials, being on the spot, should apply the deposit in a manner consistent with the principles and intentions expressed. If any difficulty arises, suspend any application of the deposit and fully explain the matter to higher authority for further orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anicut and banks — priority of repair and recognition of expense
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anicut (dam) and the banks of the Cavery are the source of the country’s prosperity, require very considerable annual expense to keep in repair, and any injury to the Anicut would essentially affect the whole country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implications: prioritize ongoing repairs and maintenance; recognize that neglect increases repair costs and can cause overflow or parching across districts. Investigate and guard against attempts to prevent or damage repairs (reports of inhabitants of adjacent country instigating damage should be pursued).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid retrospective harshness; apply equity when much time has elapsed
rubrics_metrics.description: After a great length of time has elapsed, it is highly unjust to compel the Rajah to pay supposed balances or to render a specific account of collections made long ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where records are unclear and many years have passed, favor equitable forbearance rather than strict retrospective enforcement; use local judgment to reach a fair disposition consistent with previously stated principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rule — consult records, investigate thoroughly, and report if suspending actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before deciding contested points, thoroughly examine all materials, records, and previous proceedings; if you judge it expedient to suspend execution of orders for reasons of peace and tranquillity or if difficulties arise in applying funds, transmit proceedings and the full state of facts and reasons to the Commissioners without delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory reporting and consultation requirement: local discretion is permitted for peace, but suspension must be accompanied by prompt reporting and full explanation so further orders can be given.
